## Summary

Settled the pre-registration's three open items (D24 floor gate k=6/4-of-6, D25 per-repo cap 40% with at least 3 repos, D26 band-match plus blind discrimination test at a 0.65 CI upper bound), then the freeze review found a flaw D25 could not reach and the document froze on 2026-08-10 as D29. The flaw: standingConstraintLines renders EVERY standing constraint of an initiative verbatim with the exact total in the header, so co-planted constraints are visible to each other's sessions — not just a sibling leak surface but a salience confound with a known direction, since a wall of rules plausibly makes a session more rule-attentive and deflates the rate. That is the same bias D24 had just closed, arriving through a different door. Ruled one constraint per initiative (D27), which lands on the modal historical case, 9 of 23 rule-carrying initiatives holding exactly one. D27 and D25 are jointly infeasible on the four scenario-3 sources — N_max would be 40, giving a 2.49% bound and no licence for the claim — so the host pool reopened to six repos with crisperflow and waylla (D28), lifting N_max to 70. The old pool had been selected for decision supply, a criterion scenario 4 abandoned. Two measurement corrections fell out: crisperflow carries 36 native standing constraints, so D26's rule corpus is 100 entries across three repos rather than 62 across two; and cost-report.py --project-floor silently folds archived and retired runs into its per-source means, which had inflated the floor bracket by about 50 percent. N stays open with its selection rule frozen, on the split that cost is not outcome data but spring rate is.

## Next action

Price sofar, crisperflow and waylla, and build detached snapshot clones with S7 verification for the two new hosts (4.0) before the run owner fixes N.
